public_rationale: This combines a bubble analogy with a hedged impression of an undefined group of articles. Contemporary coverage did discuss profitability, so a literal claim that such discussion never occurred would be untenable. But replacing never seem with never would unfairly strengthen the speaker's commitment. The statement cannot receive a defensible binary score as written.
limitations: The selected articles do not establish the prevalence of profitability discussion.
One article displays a later update.
The embedded company financial descriptions have not been independently graded.

our_interpretation: Hallmark expresses a resemblance or warning sign, not a specified diagnostic rule for identifying bubbles.
Glossy stories and never seem describe an undefined, hedged impression of coverage.

criteria.support_condition: No fair binary support condition exists without defining the coverage sample, the amount of profit discussion required and the proposed bubble criterion.
criteria.contradiction_condition: No fair binary contradiction condition exists for the hedged statement. Counterexamples can challenge a literal universal reading but cannot settle the stated impression.
